recipe_name: Broccoli and Potato Salad with Lemon Herb Chicken
visual_description: The salad is presented on an everyday ceramic plate, sitting on a well-used wooden dining table. Roasted baby potato halves, golden-brown and tender, are scattered among vibrant green, slightly charred broccoli florets. Small, irregularly diced chicken pieces are nestled throughout, showing a light golden sear. Halved bright red cherry tomatoes and thin slices of red onion add pops of color. The salad is casually arranged, with components naturally overlapping, and glistening lightly with a lemon-herb vinaigrette. A simple fork and a crumpled cloth napkin rest beside the plate. Warm, cozy lighting from overhead kitchen fixtures illuminates the homely scene, emphasizing the comforting textures and natural colors of the ingredients. The plate is adequately filled, leaving some negative space around the edges.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Halve baby potatoes. Toss with 15 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on baking sheet. Roast for 20 minutes.

Toss broccoli florets with 15 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Add to the baking sheet with potatoes. Continue roasting for another 15-20 minutes, until potatoes are tender and broccoli is slightly charred.
While vegetables roast, dice chicken breast into 2 cm cubes. Season with salt, pepper, and 5 ml olive oil.

Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken. Cook for 6-8 minutes, stirring occasionally, until chicken is cooked through and reaches an internal temperature of 75°C. Set aside to cool slightly.
Halve cherry tomatoes. Thinly slice red onion.
For the dressing, whisk together remaining 25 ml olive oil, juice from the lemon, Dijon mustard, and dried oregano in a small bowl. Season with salt and pepper.
In a large bowl, combine roasted potatoes, roasted broccoli, cooked chicken, halved cherry tomatoes, and sliced red onion.
Pour dressing over the salad. Toss gently to coat all ingredients.
Chop fresh parsley. Sprinkle over the salad before serving.

recipe_name: Stacked Tomato, Rice & Cheese Tortilla Bake
visual_description: A single, individual portion of a golden-baked Stacked Tomato, Rice & Cheese Tortilla Bake sits slightly off-center on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The bake is composed of several distinct layers: soft corn tortillas, fluffy rice infused with vibrant diced tomatoes and aromatic spices, and generous amounts of melted, bubbly Monterey Jack cheese, with the top layer beautifully golden and slightly crisped. A subtle pool of rich, savory tomato liquid from the bake gathers around its base. The dish is generously garnished with bright green, freshly chopped cilantro. The setting is a modern bistro: a simple, light wooden table surface, a neatly folded cotton napkin beside the plate, and a small ramekin of vibrant red salsa roja. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors. The background is softly blurred, suggesting a casual, inviting atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of authentic salsa roja or salsa verde.
Offer a dollop of crema (Mexican sour cream) or plain Greek yogurt.
Serve with a side of refried beans or black beans.

ingredients.name: Small corn or flour tortillas (approx. 15 cm diameter)
Shredded Monterey Jack or Mexican blend cheese

instructions: Preheat oven to 180 C.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Sauté minced onion until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic, cumin, chili powder, and smoked paprika. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in rice. Cook 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Add diced tomatoes (undrained) and vegetable broth. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook 15-20 minutes until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed. Season with salt and pepper.
Lightly grease a baking dish (approx. 20x20 cm).
Place one tortilla in the dish. Spread a layer of rice mixture over it. Sprinkle with a portion of shredded cheese.
Repeat layering: tortilla, rice, cheese. End with a tortilla on top, generously covered with remaining cheese.
Bake 20-25 minutes, or until cheese is melted and bubbly and edges are golden.
Let rest 5 minutes. Cut into 4 equal portions.
Serve each portion on a plate. Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro.

recipe_name: Chili-Braised Chicken Thighs with Sweet Onions
visual_description: A single portion of Chili-Braised Chicken Thighs is centrally plated on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Two rich, dark brown chicken thighs, braised to a tender, fall-off-the-bone texture, are positioned slightly overlapping. They retain their whole, rustic shape. Abundant, glossy, deeply caramelized thin onion slices are nestled around and partially beneath the chicken. A generous pour of the dark, glossy braising liquid, infused with chili and beef stock, pools around the chicken and onions. The sauce is thick, coating the ingredients. A scattering of vibrant, finely chopped fresh parsley provides a pop of green. The plate rests on a simple wooden table, with a folded cotton napkin beside it. Natural, even light illuminates the dish, highlighting its rich textures and inviting presentation.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Lightly dredge chicken in flour, shaking off excess.

Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs skin-side down until deeply golden and crisp, about 6-8 minutes. Flip and sear other side for 3-4 minutes. Remove chicken and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add thinly sliced onions to the pot. Cook, stirring occasionally, until deeply caramelized and tender, about 15-20 minutes.

While onions cook, toast dried Ancho chilies in a dry pan over medium heat for 1-2 minutes until fragrant. Remove from heat. Remove stems and seeds. Place chilies in a bowl and cover with hot water. Let rehydrate for 15 minutes.
Drain rehydrated chilies. Blend chilies with peeled garlic cloves and tomato paste until a smooth paste forms. Add a tablespoon of beef stock if needed to aid blending.
Add chili-garlic paste to the pot with caramelized onions. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in beef stock. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Add thyme sprigs and bay leaf.
Return seared chicken thighs to the pot. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged in liquid. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Cover the pot tightly. Transfer to a preheated oven at 160°C (325°F). Braise for 45-60 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and is very tender.

Remove chicken from the pot. Discard thyme sprigs and bay leaf. Skim any excess fat from the sauce. If sauce is too thin, simmer on stovetop over medium-high heat until desired consistency. Adjust seasoning.
Serve chicken with the caramelized onions and generous amounts of the braising sauce. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: For a spicier dish, add a pinch of cayenne pepper or a small amount of a hotter chili like a chipotle chili to the blending paste.

recipe_name: Slow-Roasted Beef with Fermented Red Cabbage & Root Puree
visual_description: A single portion of Slow-Roasted Beef with Fermented Red Cabbage and Root Puree is presented on a handcrafted, matte cream-colored ceramic plate with ample white space. A large, rustic chunk of deeply browned, slow-roasted beef is positioned centrally. Beside it, a distinct, smooth mound of creamy, pale beige root vegetable puree provides a comforting base. Balancing the composition, a vibrant, ruby-red pile of thinly shredded quick fermented red cabbage adds a striking contrast in color and texture. A glossy, dark brown beef reduction is elegantly drizzled over the beef and sparingly around the plate. The overall plating is minimalistic and clean, highlighting the natural beauty and texture of each ingredient. A single, fresh green thyme sprig rests gently on the beef, offering a subtle pop of color. The dish is set on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface. An undyed, natural beige linen napkin is folded neatly to the side. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene, emphasizing the rich, earthy tones of the food and natural textures of the setting. The background is clean and uncluttered, with a subtle hint of green from a distant plant, maintaining an eco-conscious aesthetic.
instructions: Preheat oven to 150°C.
Pat beef chuck dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear beef chuck on all sides until deeply browned and a crust forms. Remove beef and set aside.
Add sliced onion and whole garlic cloves to the pot. Sauté for 5 minutes until softened.
Return beef to the pot. Add beef stock and fresh thyme sprigs.
Cover the pot tightly. Transfer to the preheated oven. Slow roast for 3.5 to 4 hours, or until beef is fork-tender.
Remove beef from the pot. Strain the cooking liquid into a saucepan. Discard solids. Reduce liquid over medium-high heat until it thickens into a rich sauce. Season to taste.
For the fermented red cabbage: Thinly shred red cabbage. Place in a bowl. Add 5g of sea salt. Massage cabbage vigorously with hands for 5 minutes until it softens and releases liquid.
Stir in apple cider vinegar. Let sit at room temperature for at least 30 minutes, or up to 2 hours, for a quick ferment. Taste and adjust seasoning.
For the root puree: Peel and chop carrots, parsnips, and celeriac into 2 cm chunks.
Place chopped vegetables in a pot. Cover with water. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer until very tender, about 15-20 minutes.
Drain vegetables thoroughly. Return to the pot. Add a splash of the reduced beef stock or a tablespoon of olive oil. Mash or blend until smooth and creamy. Season with salt and pepper.

To plate: Place a generous mound of root puree off-center on each plate. Cut the beef chuck into large, natural chunks. Place one chunk beside the puree. Add a vibrant pile of the quick fermented red cabbage. Drizzle the rich beef reduction over the beef and around the plate. Garnish with a small fresh thyme sprig.

recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Roasted Broccoli and Lemon-Garlic Sauce
visual_description: A single, golden-brown pan-seared chicken breast, cooked whole, rests centrally on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken boasts a crisp, savory crust and juicy interior. Beside it, a generous portion of vibrant green roasted broccoli florets are arranged naturally, showing slightly charred edges for texture. A shimmering, pale yellow lemon-garlic butter sauce is spooned artfully over the chicken and around the plate's base, reflecting light. Fresh green parsley is sprinkled over the sauce as a garnish. The dish is presented on a simple wooden table surface, with a white cotton napkin folded neatly to the side. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's inviting colors and textures, creating a refined yet approachable presentation.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Toss broccoli florets with 30ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking tray.
Roast broccoli for 15-20 minutes until tender-crisp and slightly charred.
Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat remaining 30ml olive oil in a large oven-safe pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken breasts for 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown.
Transfer pan to preheated oven. Cook for 10-15 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken from pan. Let rest 5 minutes on a cutting board.
Return pan to medium heat. Add minced garlic and sauté 30 seconds until fragrant.
Deglaze pan with chicken stock. Scrape up any browned bits.
Stir in lemon juice and zest. Bring to a simmer.
Whisk in butter until sauce is slightly thickened. Remove from heat.
Stir in chopped parsley. Taste and adjust seasoning.
